headline: Design, supply, configure, install and commission a simple and robust industrial broadband Ethernet radio network connecting the Engineering Office to the WWTW Control Room via the SR3 high site. The solution shall support the existing Rockwell EtherNet/IP/SCADA infrastructure, provide a minimum 200–300 Mbps network throughput, use the approved 5 GHz/microwave architecture, avoid UHF telemetry/polling technology, and minimise operational and maintenance complexity.
openQuestion: Is 200–300 Mbps usable throughput per link, aggregate network capacity, or the radio's advertised nominal rate?
assumption: Until WUC answers, design to a minimum 300 Mbps measured usable TCP/IP throughput under normal operating conditions on each critical broadband link. This stops a '300 Mbps radio' that only moves 170 Mbps of real traffic from qualifying.
sr3Note: The TTA study and Rev 3 specify an omnidirectional antenna at SR3, with directional antennas at the Engineering Office and WWTW aimed at SR3. This was designed before the 200–300 Mbps requirement was known, and TTA §7.6 asks for gains and heights to be reviewed once equipment and throughput are fixed. Ask the RF contractor to prove the omni topology delivers the throughput; if it cannot, propose two directional point-to-point links at SR3 as a deviation for client approval.

items.text: 200–300 Mbps transmission capability. The client rejected the ~128 kbps Miri solution as a bottleneck.
No UHF telemetry radios. WUC discontinued that approach because of low bandwidth, polling, complexity and maintenance.
Broadband, Ethernet-style communications rather than low-speed polling telemetry.
Simple to configure and maintain; avoid complicated systems.
Robust, utility-grade installation with adequate RSSL and fade margin; no marginal paths.
WWTW Control Room, SR3 and the Engineering Office.
Central high site and repeater between the Engineering Office and WWTP.
Not allowed: inadequate margin even with a 50 m WWTP mast.
Omnidirectional at SR3; higher-gain directional antennas at the Engineering Office and WWTW, aimed at SR3.
Integrate with the existing Rockwell PLC/SCADA environment (EtherNet/IP); CGI retains PLC/SCADA integration.
Supply plus installation, configuration, onsite testing and commissioning.
Prove 300 Mbps at the modulation the link actually runs, not merely that a link closes at −80 dBm (TTA §4.3 basis).
Redo link budgets with the selected radio, legal EIRP, channel width, cable losses, interference and availability; review antenna gains and heights.
At or above the TTA minimum heights: SR3 22 m, WWTP 9 m, Engineering Office 5 m; final heights per the approved construction drawings.

process.note: The network carries operational OT data, not just a reporting dashboard. The original enquiry listed five pump stations; the current Contract 6 package is three radio stations.

philosophy.note: Simple to understand, simple to maintain, modern, high bandwidth, minimal special telemetry logic. Local plant control stays in the PLC.
